domain_context.shared_foundations: Linear algebra/complex amplitudes, probability and statistics, introductory quantum mechanics and quantum information (states, gates, measurement, entanglement), computational thinking and programming; deeper device physics, control, metrology, optics, networking or QEC are specialization-dependent.
domain_context.cross_area_outputs: A learner should be able to formulate a quantum information/measurement problem; identify applicable classical baselines and physical/platform constraints; create or characterize a quantum system; test, calibrate, compile, simulate or measure it; report resource/performance/uncertainty limits; and explain whether a claimed use is established, emerging or roadmap-only.
key_distinctions: Quantum computing, quantum sensing/metrology, and quantum networks are connected QIST branches but have distinct outputs and area choices.
Quantum key distribution is quantum communication; post-quantum cryptography is classical cryptography designed to resist quantum attacks.
QAOA/VQE, quantum machine learning, and vendor roadmap claims are not proof of general quantum advantage.
Tools/frameworks implement workflows; they are not methods, algorithms, hardware modalities, or substitutes for foundations.

area_boundary_and_outputs.expected_outputs: Mathematics, quantum information and programming feed circuit/algorithm design. Problem structure and a classical baseline constrain whether a quantum algorithm is relevant. Circuit output is transpiled/compiled to the selected QPU; hardware topology/noise/calibration feed compilation and error-control choices. Error suppression and mitigation can improve estimates on noisy runs but do not correct arbitrary errors or guarantee unbiased outputs. QEC encodes logical information, repeated syndrome measurements feed a decoder, and real-time decoding/control supports fault-tolerant computation; resource costs are part of algorithm selection. Hybrid optimization has a classical optimizer/host that supplies parameters and consumes measured expectations. Q#, OpenQASM, Qiskit, Cirq, PennyLane, CUDA-Q and provider APIs are tools/languages/frameworks with different backends, not alternatives to learning algorithms themselves.

area_boundary_and_outputs.expected_outputs: Quantum-state/control/measurement foundations and metrology/statistics support modality-specific sensor design. The target measurand and conditions (field, temperature, vibration, size, distance, bandwidth) select among sensor alternatives; those are not interchangeable just because each is quantum. Optical/electronic/vacuum/cryogenic interfaces and classical signal processing/calibration are complementary. A sensor produces a traceable measurement/uncertainty or signal stream for navigation, timing, science, medical or industrial tasks; deployment claims need comparison against classical instruments and field conditions. Networked sensing can depend on communications/entanglement infrastructure, but an individual sensor route does not require a quantum network.
